text:
maria: Anyone else seeing redwoodctl hang in our local CI container? Running `local-serve` inside docker-compose and it just pauses on startup for minutes.
ben: yep hit this this morning. container logs show it waiting for user input — no TTY so it just blocks.
ben: snippet from the log:\n```
[INFO] redwoodctl starting...\n[WARN] autoupdate available 0.9.2 -> 0.10.0\nUpdate now? (y/n)
```
maria: aha that explains why token file never gets written — process never proceeds to the login step.
sam: Workaround I used: set `REDWOODCTL_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1` in the docker env. Stops the prompt and startup continues.\nAlso `export TERM=dumb` helps in some CI systems.
leo: FYI there's no `--no-update` flag in the latest stable (0.9.2). We have an in-progress change in the dev branch to respect `REDWOODCTL_AUTOUPDATE=false`, but not released yet. PR reference: #432 (internal).
ben: Quick hack if you can't set env: run the command with `unbuffer` or `script -q -c 'redwoodctl login --headless' /dev/null` but not ideal.
ci-bot: incident:devex-321 created and assigned to @maria and @leo :rotating_light:
maria: @leo can we default to skipping autoupdate in non-interactive sessions (non-TTY / CI)? That would avoid a bunch of flaky local CI runs and headless docker setups.
leo: Yep, plan: detect isatty and common CI env vars (CI=true, GITHUB_ACTIONS, TERM=dumb) and treat non-interactive as 'skip update' with a single log line pointing to `REDWOODCTL_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE`. I'll open a tiny PR to change behavior and add a changelog note.
sam: Also let's add a clear note in the local-serve sample docker-compose.yml and the onboarding docs about how to run headless (env var + volume mount for ~/.redwoodctl). I can PR a docs patch.
maria: Workaround for now (copy-paste): in docker-compose.yml under the service set:\n```
environment:\n  - REDWOODCTL_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1\n  - TERM=dumb
volumes:\n  - ~/.redwoodctl:/home/redwood/.redwoodctl
```
ben: Also adding a quick check in our sample app start script: if `tty` is absent, warn and skip update. Saves folks from debugging.
leo: I'll include a unit test that simulates non-TTY to prevent regressions. ETA: today.
maria: thanks y'all. once PR lands can we backport to the 0.9.x branch? That's what our infra uses.
leo: yes, will include backport to the 0.9.x patch branch if tests look good.
sam: :thumbsup: also opened a tiny issue to surface a clearer error when redwoodctl can't write the token file due to permission/volume problems — that was another confusing symptom here.
maria: perfect. leaving the incident open until docs + patch are merged.
